scope: Read-only review; no hardware motion, SDK installation, shared SDK/H0 edits, training, or remote writes.

installed_sdk.hardware: Piper H, firmware parsed as v189

decision.local_fallback: Use the existing Piper H physical drag-teaching capability to capture a source trajectory, annotate gripper events, and replay it through the unique pyAgxArm sender. Collect the training episode during successful real external replay.
decision.source_data_not_training: Dragged joint/width feedback is trajectory-source data. It must not be relabeled as commands. Teacher-hand images and failed or interrupted replays remain outside the first success-only training split.
decision.internal_replay: The physical double-click controller playback is documented, but no reviewed source proves it broadcasts complete, timed, fresh 0x155/0x156/0x157/0x159 commands on host CAN. A parser being able to decode those IDs is insufficient evidence. Do not promise controller-internal playback can produce traceable 7D actions.
decision.no_new_teleop_hardware: No UArm, second arm, VR controller, or teaching pendant purchase required for this plan.
decision.availability: The repository has passive RGB/state recording and model dataset code, but lacks a complete ready-to-run teach-marker/replay/real-action episode collector. Codex must add a small local module before providing the executable command line.

official_evidence.title: PIPER H 用户手册
findings: Single-click switches drag trajectory recording on/off; green steady during recording and lamp off when stopped.
Double-click after a recording starts one internal replay; green flashes at approximately 500 ms.
Each new built-in recording replaces the previous one; built-in recording is limited to three minutes.
After teaching, confirm lamp off, switch to standby, then CAN control.
official_evidence.caution: Do not copy full fetched manual into project deliverables; cite source and summarize only.

findings: The standard gripper/teaching-device panel independently controls enable, spacing and torque, and reports actual gripper values.
A teaching device is an optional separate end effector. The manual does not establish that this user's ordinary energized gripper can safely be hand-forced.
The desktop trajectory library can import/export/edit trajectories, but reviewed text does not establish export of the physical-button internal recording with full image/command timing.
Official example records measured joint state and measured gripper opening with elapsed times in CSV.
It waits for teaching mode, asks Enter to record, samples around 100 Hz, and writes only changed poses.
It is a trajectory recorder, not an RGB/action training-data collector.
Official example replays CSV as explicit host JointCtrl and GripperCtrl commands.
It relies on piper_sdk C_PiperInterface_V2 rather than installed pyAgxArm.
The example defaults to speed percentage 100 and includes EmergencyStop/recovery and zero-position waiting. Do not run or port these defaults unchanged to the current commissioned Piper H.
move_j accepts six joint angles in radians and submits its command messages; get_joint_angles and get_arm_status provide measured feedback.
No ordinary drag-record/playback high-level public method was found in this pinned driver; leader/follower-specific methods are not a reason to reconfigure this single arm.
move_js is a distinct immediate-response mode with explicit shock/instability warning; do not substitute it for the commissioned MOVE_J path.
Received 0x155, 0x156 and 0x157 decode into leader_joint_12, leader_joint_34 and leader_joint_56; this only describes received messages.
move_gripper_m(value, force) sends absolute opening in meters and force in newtons using status_code=1.
get_gripper_ctrl_states returns an optional cached decoded command only if received; no query guaranteeing internal playback target extraction.
disable_gripper/calibrate_gripper are separate maintenance functions, not a general requirement for every teaching episode.

proposed_operator_workflow: Prepare one lightweight matte block that fits the already measured gripper opening, and a fixed shallow tray. Keep the block and approach visible from the fixed wrist camera/start pose. Record camera mount and calibration identifiers.
Start existing passive RGB/CAN recording and the new trajectory/event collector. The teaching phase does not issue joint or gripper motion commands.
With lamp off, single-click the physical teaching button; confirm green steady and actual teaching mode. In the proposed UI press Enter to start source recording.

Guide the arm smoothly through: safe start -> pregrasp above block -> grasp pose -> vertical lift -> above tray -> release pose -> retreat. At grasp pose and release pose, mark CLOSE and OPEN intent with keyboard; these marks do not move the jaws during teaching.

The gripper can remain at the previously verified open width throughout source teaching. Do not hand-force its jaws. No successful grasp is claimed during this pass; the physical task success will be checked in replay.
End source recording; single-click physical button back to lamp off. Preserve the source trajectory immediately because another built-in recording overwrites controller memory.

Codex validates the captured path, joint limits, step size, speed/acceleration budget and gripper event order; use the existing verified standby->CAN handoff and sole-sender lock. Do not reuse old example EmergencyStop/reset routines.

Reset the block to the recorded placement, keep hands outside the working path, then start one replay from its real verified start pose. The unique sender executes the captured/interpolated joint path, holds at the grasp marker while issuing real CLOSE, then lifts/transfers, holds at release while issuing real OPEN, then retreats.

Before the first object-bearing replay of each materially new path, complete a low-speed real empty-workspace traversal with the same gripper events; verify clearance, cable motion, timing and normal pause/hold. This is an actual trajectory check, not synthetic training data or a policy capacity test.

During replay save all raw wrist RGB, real joint/gripper feedback, exact actual targets and send outcomes. With an object in the jaws, measured width need not reach the closed target; record target and measured width separately.

Inspect the complete video and feedback, mark actual outcome: successful grasp, lift, placement, release, retreat, no manual rescue. Admit only complete successful, cleanly logged episodes to the initial training split. Keep failures/interruptions with reason but exclude them from initial success cloning.
Change the block placement and teach a matching new trajectory before replaying at that placement. Do not blindly move the block and replay an old fixed joint path.
Finish by normal hold and report actual final arm mode/enable/gripper state. Ctrl+C, generic process killing, disabling drives and emergency damping are not interchangeable with a normal pause.

minimal_module_requirements.location: Only π repository tasks/piper_real_single_v1; names/CLI finalized by Codex after implementation.
source_capture: timestamped q_source_rad[6], measured gripper width, mode, source feedback IDs, session/boot IDs
markers with source timestamp/index, grasp/release stage, intended gripper target; raw source retained
record stationary samples, start pose and terminal hold explicitly; do not just port the official changed-only CSV loop
use existing passive receiver, not a second active controller
execution: one sender and the existing shared motion lock; pyAgxArm MOVE_J only
per-tick requested and post-limits/quantization applied targets, held gripper target provenance
send_bus.send interception below SDK wrappers, including gripper commands; exceptions and partial groups are not successful targets
real-time feedback directly from receiver events, not the 2-second-flush viewer CSV
first replay uses current verified limits; the historical 2-degree calibration move bound does not authorize a full pick/place trajectory
no model is necessary to collect these demonstrations; the teacher path is the controller source
action_schema: observation receive monotonic_ns, camera header timestamp, actual feedback receive timestamps/IDs and ages
command_due_ns, submit_start_ns, submit_end_ns; each CAN ID/data/submission result/exception
measured q_rad[6], measured width_m, tracking error, mode, drive enable/error/motion status
training_eligible and reason after episode QA, task instruction, placement/session split group
timing_checks: RGB/source-header-to-receive distribution remains separately reported; received clock is not exposure synchronization
RGB/joint/gripper receive intervals and queue drops, full-joint CAN group span
observation/state age at each actual command submission, deadline jitter, send latency and partial-send count
time from real target submission to feedback changes and subsequent settled tracking error
20 Hz dataset is a 50 ms label grid, not an asserted policy inference rate
join only by timestamps on the same host and boot; do not relabel feedback or replay intent as a successfully submitted command

collection_budget.nature: Engineering pilot proposal, not a minimum guaranteed by a paper or a promise of policy success.
collection_budget.initial_validation: First collect 3-5 complete successful replay episodes for commissioning and inspect full video, actual command provenance and dynamic time alignment. Later formal successful local demonstrations are explicitly authorized for training after QA; no further permission gate.
collection_budget.first_formal_batch: Engineering starting target: 30-50 diverse successful complete task episodes; for a concrete 50-episode batch use 40 train and 10 validation, grouping by taught source trajectory and physical placement/session. This is not 50 repeats of one identical path and not an official guaranteed minimum.
collection_budget.variety: About 10 distinct taught block placements within the verified wrist-visible reachable area, with several real replays per placement, plus modest natural lighting/object orientation/start-pose variation only when the executed trajectory is still appropriate. Same trajectory repeated at an identical setup is not independent diversity.
collection_budget.evaluation: Reserve additional real reset conditions/placements for closed-loop policy testing, separate from demonstration training/validation; count successes over explicit attempts and record intervention/failure phase.
collection_budget.escalation: If the first task does not learn or generalize, add data at observed failure states/placements rather than promising the initial count is sufficient. Keep π0 and π0.5 comparisons on the same dataset split and protocol.

fallback: If continuous drag capture is awkward, use keyframe capture at the same grasp/lift/place/retreat stages plus conservatively interpolated replay, preserving human-taught source and real replay targets.
If gripper action during teaching mode cannot be verified, keep it as event annotation only; actuate only after documented standby->CAN transition.
If no safe valid source path has been captured, do not invent angles or run arbitrary example poses; obtain poses through the existing physical teaching method.
Do not block the local route on proving that controller-internal double-click playback exposes action commands. External replay already supplies their provenance.
publication_note: Compact review evidence. Local retrieval paths may refer to analysis-only source material that was not published; see README.md for the exact published subset. No complete source episode or training dataset is included.
